name: Margaret
made_for: Osteoarthritis in both knees and her hands
goal: Spend a morning in the garden again without paying for it all evening
sample_note: This is a sample plan for a made-up reader, to show what a Personal Joint Plan looks like. Your own plan is written from your answers.
note: Margaret, thank you for telling us about your mornings. The 40 stiff minutes before your knees wake up. The jar lids. The way the garden used to be the best part of your day, and now it's the part you put off.
This plan doesn't ask you to change your life. It fits around the one you have. Coffee at 7, the radio, your sister's call on Thursdays. We built everything around those.
You told us the heating pad helps and glucosamine didn't. So we kept the warmth and left the pills out. You also said you'd rather move than sit. Good. That's the strongest thing in this plan.
Start small. Some days you'll do all three anchors. Some days one. Both count.
how_to_use: Read pages 3 and 4 first. That's your day.
Stick the two fridge cards on the fridge.
Tick the 30-day sheet each time you do an anchor.
Reply to our check-in emails. That's how your plan gets better.

anchors.title: Warm up before you stand
anchors.why: Five minutes under the covers so your knees aren't cold and stiff when they take your weight.

anchors.title: The garden, in short visits
anchors.why: Fifteen minutes on a kneeling pad, then rest. Short visits you can repeat beat one long one you pay for.

video.title: How to stay active with osteoarthritis

anchors.title: Six chair stands after lunch
anchors.why: Strong thigh muscles carry weight your knees don't have to.

video.title: Yoga for arthritis: chair yoga for mobility

steps: Circle each ankle 5 times each way.
Pump your feet: point the toes, then pull them back, 10 times.
Slide one heel up toward you and back down, 5 times each leg.
Sit on the edge of the bed. Make 10 soft fists, opening your fingers wide each time.
Warm shower, or a heat pad on the stiffer knee for 15 minutes.
Hands in a bowl of warm water for one minute, then touch your thumb to each fingertip.
Garden for 15 minutes on a kneeling pad or a low stool.
Come in, sit, and wrap the knee in a warm towel for 10 minutes.
If you feel good, go back out for another 15. Stop while you still feel fine.
Six slow chair stands from your kitchen chair, hands on the table. Count 3 up and 3 down.
A 10-minute walk to the mailbox and around the block.
Rub cayenne (capsaicin) cream on the sorest knee. Wash your hands after.
Five slow breaths in bed: in for 4, out for 6.

weeks.title: Week 1. Just the anchors.
weeks.text: Bed moves every morning, one 15-minute garden visit, and 4 chair stands after lunch. Nothing more. You're building the habit, not the muscle.

weeks.title: Week 2. Add the walk.
weeks.text: Keep the anchors and add the 10-minute walk after lunch. Chair stands go up to 5.

weeks.title: Week 3. Two garden visits.
weeks.text: Try two 15-minute visits with a warm-towel rest between. Chair stands go up to 6.

weeks.title: Week 4. Make it yours.
weeks.text: Keep what helped, drop what didn't, and tell us at your check-in. We'll write your next steps.

checkins.what: How are the morning moves and the garden visits going?
What feels easier, and what still bothers you?
Your plan for the month after this one.

comforts_intro: You told us warmth helps. These build on that, in the order we'd try them.

comforts.name: 1. Warm and cool water for your hands
comforts.how: Warm water for 3 minutes, cold for 30 seconds, three times, ending on cold. Then open and close your hands while they're loose. Great before opening jars.

comforts.name: 2. Cayenne cream for your knee
comforts.how: A thin layer on the sorest knee 3 or 4 times a day. It stings for the first week or two, then the relief builds. Give it 3 weeks before you decide.

comforts.name: 3. A castor oil compress at night
comforts.how: Soft cotton soaked in castor oil, wrapped round the knee, covered and left on overnight. Barbara O'Neill swears by it. It's soothing and costs very little.

comforts.name: You can skip
comforts.how: Glucosamine. You tried it and felt nothing, and the biggest studies agree with you.

food_intro: You eat toast and coffee for breakfast, a sandwich at lunch and pasta most nights. These swaps keep the foods you like and add more of what's kind to joints.

food_swaps.to: whole-grain toast with mashed avocado, or oats with berries and a spoon of ground flaxseed
a hummus and roasted-vegetable sandwich, or lentil soup with a slice of good bread
pasta with tomatoes, olive oil, garlic and spinach
a handful of walnuts and a bowl of tart cherries, fresh or frozen
Celtic salt, a little at a time. Check with your doctor first, since you take a blood-pressure medicine

drinks: Keep your morning coffee. Add a glass of water before each meal, about 8 glasses a day in all. Warm water with lemon is a nice start to the day.
flare: Do half of what you'd normally do. Don't stop completely.
Cold pack wrapped in a cloth on a puffy, hot knee, 15 minutes. Warmth if it's just stiff.
Skip the garden, keep the bed moves.
Five slow breaths, out longer than in.
Ask your sister to bring the groceries on Thursday.
When it settles, build back up over a few days.
call_doctor: A knee turns hot, red and very swollen, mostly with a fever.
You fall and can't put weight on your leg.
A bad spell isn't easing after a week.

day_tips.tip: Today, just do your three things. That's all. Small and steady beats big and rare. Tick each one as you go.
Stiff joints like warmth first. A warm shower or a heat pack for 15 minutes makes your first moves easier. Warm what is stiff, cool what is swollen.
Drink a glass of water before each meal today. Joints and the cushions inside them need water to stay soft. Warm water with lemon is a nice start to the morning.
A little soreness after moving is normal. If you're sorer than usual for more than two hours after, do a bit less next time. Less, not nothing.

video.title: How to stay active with osteoarthritis

day_tips.tip: Breathe in for 4, out for 6. Do it five times. A long breath out tells your body it's safe, and tight muscles around sore joints start to let go.
Rest your hands in warm water for one minute. Then touch your thumb to each fingertip. Do this before you open jars or button a coat.
Look at your tick sheet. Every tick is a small win. Today, reply to our check-in email and tell us which thing felt easiest.
Your thigh muscles carry weight your knees don't have to. Chair stands build them. Slow is better than fast. Count three up and three down.

video.title: Yoga for arthritis: chair yoga for mobility

day_tips.tip: Add one more plant to one meal today. Beans in your soup, spinach in your pasta, berries on your oats. Plants help calm the swelling inside sore joints.

day_tips.theme: Stop while it still feels good
day_tips.tip: On a good day it's tempting to do everything. Pick your amount and stop there. You'll feel better tomorrow, and the day after.

video.title: Yoga for arthritis: healthy sitting and standing

day_tips.tip: Five minutes of walking counts. So does the hallway on a rainy day. Walk after a meal or a warm shower, when joints are looser.
Soak soft cotton in castor oil, wrap it round your sorest joint, cover it and leave it on overnight. It's warm, calming, and costs very little.
Olive oil, walnuts, ground flaxseed and avocado bring the good fats your joints like. Add a spoon of ground flaxseed to breakfast today.
Two weeks in. What feels a little easier than day 1? Reply to our check-in email and tell us. Your plan for the next two weeks changes to match.

day_tips.theme: Kind to your joints all day
day_tips.tip: Carry bags on your forearm, use two hands instead of one, and slide heavy things instead of lifting. Small changes save a lot of strain.
Hold the kitchen counter and stand with your feet close together for 20 seconds while the kettle boils. Balance gets better with practice at any age.
Capsaicin cream comes from chili peppers. A thin layer on a sore knee 3 or 4 times a day can ease pain after a week or two. Wash your hands after.
Go to bed and get up at the same time, even on weekends. A steady sleep time turns the pain alarm down.
Add a pinch of turmeric with a little black pepper to soup or rice, or a few slices of fresh ginger to hot water. Kind, warm spices from your own kitchen.
Ten minutes of morning daylight lifts your mood and helps your body make vitamin D. Sit by a bright window if it's cold out.

day_tips.tip: Three weeks of small steps. That's a habit now. Today, notice one thing your joints let you do that felt harder a month ago.

video.title: Yoga for arthritis: 5 classic poses, made easier

day_tips.tip: Ask someone for one clear bit of help this week, like carrying the laundry upstairs. Most people want to help and just need to know how.

video.title: Yoga for arthritis: healthy sitting and standing

day_tips.tip: Warm water for 3 minutes, cold for 30 seconds, three times, ending on cold. Great for hands and feet. Move them while they're loose.
Swap one sweet thing today: cookies for walnuts and tart cherries, soda for water with lemon. Less sugar, calmer joints.
A bad day doesn't undo the good ones. Do half, not nothing. Cold if hot, warm if stiff. Then build back up over a few days.
Walk with a friend, or call someone while you march in your chair. Moving is easier and more fun with company.
Print the doctor sheet in your plan and take it to your next visit. Clear notes help your doctor help you faster.
Look at your tick sheet and your pain numbers. Reply to our check-in email and tell us what you'd like to keep, drop, and work on next.

day_tips.tip: Tie each habit you want to keep to something you already do. After coffee, bed moves. After lunch, chair stands. Small hooks keep habits going.
You did it. Open My Plan to see your 30-day report and your certificate. Then keep going, at your own pace.

family: Margaret's knees are stiffest for the first 40 minutes of the day. Plan visits and calls for later in the morning.
Offer to carry, not to take over. A heavy watering can or the grocery bags are perfect jobs to share.
Ask how the garden is going, not how the arthritis is.
On a bad day, bring the groceries on Thursday without being asked twice.
If you'd like to help more, read our free guide for sons and daughters at myhingecare.com/free-guide-parent.html.

doctor.joints: Both knees, worse on the left. Fingers and thumbs, mostly in the morning.
doctor.pain: About 5 out of 10 on a usual day.
doctor.tried: Heating pad (helps). Glucosamine (no change). Walking short distances (helps).
doctor.doing_now: Morning bed moves, short garden visits, chair stands, cayenne cream, castor oil compress.
